ONE ROW PER REFUSAL, NOT PER FILE, and the block-level refusal is per block — a manifest whose `devDependencies` is malformed still contributes every package its `dependencies` block declares, and `detail` names the block that was refused. PRESENT ONLY WHEN IT HAS A MEMBER, which is the one place in this document that asymmetry is taken: an empty array on every tree would rewrite two golden census documents to say nothing, and what this closes is the case where something DID go wrong and the output said nothing. Added 2026-08-28, because `dependency_inventory: []` from a manifest that could not be read was indistinguishable from `dependency_inventory: []` from a tree with no npm manifest at all. Measured over the 3,507 package.json files of the 98-tree corpus: 0 fail JSON.parse and 0 carry a BOM, so it is absent on every tree read so far. `findings.json`'s `stats.manifests_not_usable` carries the count.

file.description: Path relative to the scan root, exactly as the walker produced it.

reason.description: parse-failed: JSON.parse refused the file. block-not-an-object: the file parsed and a runtime dependency block held something that is not an object, so `Object.entries` over it would have produced one entry per character of a string - six packages named 0 to 5 out of `"dependencies": "stripe"`, each marked declared_only. `no-dependency-block` (2026-09-03) is a `Package.resolved` that parses as JSON and carries no `pins` array in either the v1 (`object.pins`) or the v2/v3 (`pins`) position: a manifest this census opened and took nothing from, which is a different sentence from a tree with no lockfile.

detail.description: What the runtime said, or which block held what shape. Cut at 300 characters.

stats.description: What the census covered. Needed to tell a clean repository apart from a census that did not run.

files_matched.description: Files that produced at least one fact.

by_collector.description: Facts produced per collector, keyed by collector name. A collector sitting at zero is either a clean repository or a broken pattern, and this is the only place in the output where that difference is visible.

packages_declared.description: Packages declared in a `dependencies` or `optionalDependencies` block. THE RUNTIME POPULATION, NOT `dependency_inventory`'s, which also carries `devDependencies` and `peerDependencies` since 2026-08-28 and is therefore longer on most npm trees. The narrower count is kept because this minus `packages_with_call_sites` is `declared_only_dependencies.length`, an identity the next field states and a consumer can check.

packages_with_call_sites.description: Of those, how many anything actually imports. The gap is declared_only_dependencies.

packages_declared_only_not_read.description: Of declared_only_dependencies, those carrying call_sites_not_read. Absent at 0.

identifiers_not_requests.description: URLs that name a vocabulary rather than a destination (JSON-LD contexts, XML namespaces). Counted rather than dropped in silence, so that a suppression stays checkable.

manifests_marked_not_published.description: Manifests in the tree marked unpublishable. Only the shallowest few reach the facts list: in a monorepo a nested private workspace package says nothing about whether the product is supplied, and one repository produced 476 of them. The total is here so the cap is countable rather than silent.

files_not_text.description: Files the census opened and refused because their bytes are not text - a NUL inside the first 4096 characters, the walker's own test, imported rather than restated. Since 2026-09-03 no collector asks about a file's extension, so this readability check is the only capability test left in front of them. ABSENT WHERE IT IS 0, which is every tree the shipped pipeline scans, since the walker has already applied the identical test; emitted when it fires, because a refusal nobody can count is a refusal nobody can check.

pillar1Status.description: Whether the pillar-1 join ran, expressed as two mutually exclusive branches so that the not-computed case has to carry a reason.

oneOf.description: The join ran, against the findings file named here.

source.description: Path of the findings.json that was read.

scan_id.description: Scan those findings came from, so the two halves can be shown to belong to the same investigation.

target.description: Root that scan was run against. A value differing from this run's target means the two halves are describing different trees, and the overlaps mean nothing.

candidates.description: QUESTIONS in the findings file, not rows of its `candidates` array. A group the scanner split because it carried more locations than one adjudicating agent reads is one candidate emitted as several records, and counting the records makes this number move on an unchanged repository the day the bound ships. `candidate_records` is the other number.

candidate_records.description: Rows of the findings file's `candidates` array. Equal to `candidates` unless a group was split, and present so a reader who counts the rows can reconcile the two rather than guess which one this document means. Optional: a document written before the split existed carries only `candidates`, and the two were the same number then.

locations.description: Locations across those candidates - the number of places that could possibly overlap.

oneOf.description: The join did not run. The reason is mandatory so that this state is never mistaken for a join that found no overlaps.

reason.description: Why the join did not run, in words - typically that no --findings argument was supplied, or that the file named could not be read.

walkerExclusion.description: One exclusion the walker made, aggregated by reason and directory.

dir.description: Directory the exclusion applies to, relative to the scan root.

files.description: Files excluded, or null where the tree was skipped without descending, so that "not counted" is never read as "none".

examples.description: A few example paths, so the exclusion can be judged without re-running the walk.

contentMatch.description: A file discovery reached, with the phrases that matched it. Used for both populations: `content_scan.matched` holds the ones that were offered as candidate declarations, and `content_scan.screened` the ones that were not - either because they cleared the marker threshold and did not read like a document, or because their bytes are not text.

markers.description: The phrases that matched. EMPTY where the file was screened before it was ever read for phrases - a file whose bytes are not text carries no markers, and `minItems: 1` was removed on 2026-09-02 so that such an entry can be written down rather than dropped for failing validation.

screened_reason.description: Why a file was screened when no shape was measured, in words a reader can act on. It carries ONE OF THREE DIFFERENT STATEMENTS AND THEY MUST NOT BE READ AS ONE (corrected 2026-09-03): the bytes were read and hold a NUL, so the file is not text; the walker refused the file for its EXTENSION and never opened it, so nothing here says anything about its bytes; or the file is over the walker's size ceiling and was not read, which usually means readable text this run does not have. None of the three is a statement about what the file IS, which is why each is written down rather than acted on silently, and --policy <path> still reads the file as a supplied document.

screened_label.description: The same decision in two or three words, for a listing: 'not text', 'not read (binary extension - the bytes were never opened)', 'not read (over the size ceiling)'. Present only where screened_reason is. It exists so that a console line and the JSON cannot come to describe one refusal differently - the first version of the console printed 'not text' for all three, which stated a byte fact about a decision taken from a name.

contentShape.description: What the content pass measured about a file that cleared the marker threshold, and which confirming route decided whether it is a document or a file that mentions legal phrases. THE REPAIR IS A CONFIRMING CLAUSE BESIDE THE THRESHOLD, never a narrower threshold and never an extension exclusion, because subtraction is the only operation that can create a miss and this project has built a fixture for a real policy kept in a message catalogue and has not yet observed one in a scanned repository. A file must clear the threshold AND be document-shaped, and document-shaped has three independent routes of which any one is enough: the file is mostly sentences, or every marker sits beside sentences, or the file is short enough that reading it costs nothing. Measured over the fourteen catalogues and five real documents, prose_char_ratio is 0.024-0.049 on the catalogues and 0.455-0.930 on the documents. A SCREENED FILE IS NOT DROPPED: it is named in content_scan.screened[] with these numbers and its markers, and --policy <path> puts it back into the run as an explicitly supplied document. Emitted on every run from 2026-09-02; optional so that an input written before that date still validates, and absent means the file was never measured rather than measured and found shapeless.

prose_char_ratio.description: Characters of prose divided by characters in the file. A prose line is one that, with markup tags removed, is at least 40 characters long and holds at least 8 words - a sentence rather than a label, a key, a tag or a record separator - or, in a script that does not separate words with spaces, a dense enough run of its characters. FROM 2026-09-02 A PROSE LINE THAT IS A CATALOGUE RECORD DOES NOT COUNT TOWARDS THE NUMERATOR (hole 3 of the second real-repository run). `"legal.intro": "...a full sentence..."`, `msgstr "..."`, `<source>...</source>`, or a whole minified object of such pairs, is a record whatever its value says, and a file made of them is a record set. The denominator is untouched, so a real document's ratio does not move - measured on that repository, every declaration's ratio is identical to three decimals and every locale catalogue's falls from 0.19-0.99 to 0.00. THE DISCOUNT IS CONFINED TO THIS FIELD: the neighbourhood and passage routes read the undiscounted prose lines, which is what keeps a policy kept INSIDE a message catalogue and what keeps the space-less-script repair of the same day intact.

record_value_lines.description: Sentence-length lines that are a key and a quoted value and nothing else, and therefore do not count towards prose_char_ratio. Emitted so the ratio can be disputed from the record: a catalogue of full sentences reports hundreds of these beside a ratio near zero, and a real document reports none. Emitted on every run from 2026-09-02; optional so that an input written before that date still validates, and absent means the file predates the record-shape discount rather than having been measured and found to hold no records.

markers_with_prose_nearby.description: Markers whose line has a prose line within ten lines either side of it.

markers_matched.description: Markers this file matched, which is what markers_with_prose_nearby is out of.

document_shaped.description: Whether at least one confirming route held. False means the file is named in content_scan.screened[] instead of being offered as a candidate declaration.

reason.description: Which route decided it, or why none did, in words a reader can act on.

storeDeclaration.description: One store declaration, in the store's own taxonomy. Unknown identifiers pass through verbatim with no label - the parser never invents a meaning.

tracking.description: Apple's NSPrivacyTracking. Absent where the key is missing - missing is not false.

tracking_domains.description: Domains the app declares it contacts for tracking. The census's outbound hosts are the code-side counterpart.

rows.description: Play CSV only: the raw rows. Column meanings are deliberately not interpreted by the deterministic layer, because a guessed mapping that is wrong would put words in the developer's declaration.

problems.description: What could not be understood in THIS file: a malformed plist, a documented key holding the wrong kind of value, an entry with no identifier. Non-empty is a fact about the declaration, not an error of the run, and is meant to be usable as "look at this one".

notes.description: Decisions the parser made that are true of every file of the kind and say nothing about this one - Play rows carried uninterpreted, an unrecognised identifier passed through with no label, a manifest found inside a vendored dependency tree. Split out of `problems` on 2026-07-28, because one note emitted on every Play CSV ever parsed made `problems.length > 0` true of all of them and therefore useless as an attention signal.

label.description: Human-readable name, present only where the identifier is a known one.

categories.description: The census axis this declared collection bears on: collection, plus recipients where the entry is declared as tracking.

dependencyDeclaration.description: One manifest's statement about one package: the version it names, the line it names it on, and the block it names it in.

file.description: The manifest, relative to the scan root.

line.description: The line the package's key is written on, 1-based. 1 where the key could not be located in the file's text.

version.description: The version range AS DECLARED. Not resolved, not normalised, not compared with anything.

field.description: WHICH BLOCK OF THAT MANIFEST DECLARES IT. Owner ruling, 2026-08-28: the census reads all four blocks and every declaration says which one it came from, so a package declared in `dependencies` and again in `devDependencies` carries two entries with two lines and two versions. A FACT ABOUT THE MANIFEST, NOT A VERDICT ABOUT THE PACKAGE — a build-time package's data flows happen at build or CI time, which is a different moment from the product's runtime and not an absent one. `bundledDependencies` is not a value here because it is not read: it is an array of names rather than a name-to-version map, and its members are declared in one of the four above anyway. SWIFT/APPLE BLOCKS ADDED 2026-09-03: `spm-dependencies` (a `Package.swift` `dependencies:` list), `pods` (a `Podfile`'s `pod` lines) and `xcodegen-packages` (an XcodeGen `project*.yml` `packages:` block) are DIRECT declarations, what a developer wrote, and are read exactly as `dependencies` is. `spm-resolved` (`Package.resolved`) and `pods-resolved` (`Podfile.lock`) are a RESOLVER'S OUTPUT over the whole transitive graph and reach this inventory and nothing else: `declared_only_dependencies` and the `facts` dependency rows are drawn from the direct blocks only, because "declared and imported from nowhere" is the ordinary state of a transitive pin and publishing that sentence about each one would turn the anti-false-accusation half of this record into a machine for making false statements about a developer's code.

ecosystem.description: WHICH MANIFEST FAMILY this declaration was read from. A label on the record, never an input to any judgement. It exists so an empty inventory is readable as a statement about the formats that were parsed: before 2026-09-03 only `package.json` was, and a pure Swift/SwiftPM tree produced an empty inventory that a reader could not tell from a product declaring nothing.

dependencyInventoryEntry.description: One declared dependency, as the manifest and the tree state it. Facts only: no severity, no confidence, no vendor classification beyond the name the manifest writes. A declaration is not a transfer; the absence of a call site is not the absence of use; and only package.json is parsed, so an empty inventory is a statement about npm manifests and never about the product.

package.description: The package name, exactly as the manifest writes it.

declared.description: Every declaration of it, in walk order: one entry per manifest AND per block. More than one in a monorepo, and they can name different versions.

call_site_count.description: Call sites found, EXACT, counted before call_sites is truncated.

declared_only.description: true where call_site_count is 0. Written on every entry rather than only where it is true, so the marker cannot be confused with a producer that stopped writing it. READ IT BESIDE declared[].field, ALWAYS. Since 2026-09-03 this inventory also carries RESOLVED declarations - spm-resolved (Package.resolved) and pods-resolved (Podfile.lock) - which are a resolver's output over the whole TRANSITIVE graph, and for most of a transitive graph "declared and imported from nowhere" is the ORDINARY state rather than an observation (15 of one real iOS tree's 21 rows, all 39 of another's). declared_only_dependencies and the facts dependency rows are drawn from the DIRECT blocks only for that reason, and this boolean is the one place the resolved rows still carry the sentence. It is a fact about call sites, never an accusation about a package: a consumer that reports "declared and unused" from this field without filtering on `field` will publish that sentence about packages nobody claimed to import. Where call_sites_not_read is present beside it, lines that could hold a call site were not read and the absence is not known.

call_sites_not_read.description: Present only where declared_only is true and lines that could hold a call site were not read: the import pass reads every readable file, so a line past the line ceiling anywhere in the tree (named in files_long_lines_not_read), a file the per-file budget stopped before its import pass ended (named in files_stopped_for_time) or a file that could not be read leaves the absence NOT KNOWN. No call site was found in what was read; whether the package is imported is not known, and a reader says not read, never not imported. Absent where every such line was read.

lines_past_ceiling.description: Lines past the line ceiling, emptied before the import pass, in files it read.

files.description: Files not read to their end by the import pass: holding those lines, stopped for time before it ended, or not readable.

call_sites.description: Up to three call sites, file and line only. A sample, never the count.
